study: Shoreline Theatre S18 first-draft authoring, 25 November 2026
scope: Locally distilled authoring instructions. Upstream separates modeling, risk proposals, human risk/oracle approval and export. This trial evaluates unpublished drafts and imports no approved risk, plan or case.
protocol: Four new assistant model sessions with no shared conversation history. Each received only its native provider messages. The nominal 1–10 project range was held constant and the brief requested five cases in 500 narrative words. Pairs were h1/h2 and h4/h3. Graders saw anonymous native normalized drafts before treatment assignment was disclosed.
transport: The first loopback invocation captured native requests. Its processes closed at assistant handoff before delivery. A second local invocation verified the entire outgoing request and message bytes against the original, then returned the unedited first model answer to the native parser. Each subject produced one answer. No Tesbo project model allocation, source retrieval, database write, publication or test execution took place.

baseGenerationInput.story: Shoreline Theatre is releasing seat exchanges at the box office and a Call action on the standby desk. Write the release test cases for the team.
baseGenerationInput.context:
Release S18. Box office QA handover, 25 November.

Ticket BOX-17. A cashier can prepare exchange offers for an existing booking at either sales desk and confirm an offer. An offer records its own reference, the booking, old/new seats and the service charge. BOX-17 screen copy lists two possible confirmations: Exchange complete and Refresh offer. The cashier can reopen a booking, including its assigned seat, from another desk.

OPERATIONS 8.2 (in force). Issuing a replacement offer retires every earlier offer for the same booking. A retired offer cannot complete an exchange. The seats shown on the current booking change only upon completion. Finance reconciliation links one exchange receipt and one service-charge entry to each completed offer reference. Finance can look up a reference in either register even if it has no rows. There is no charge to obtain or replace an offer.

Ticket FOH-42. A steward selects a standby booking and presses Call. The list refreshes in place as new bookings arrive. It is sorted by membership tier and then arrival minute. The row position can move during a selection. Several patrons may use the same display name. The desk log and booking detail identify bookings by reference.

FRONT OF HOUSE 4.1 (in force). Call is attached to the selected booking. Calling it moves that booking from Waiting to Called and writes a notice for its registered contact to the dispatch outbox. Other waiting bookings are left alone. The outbox can be read by booking reference and recipient. Calling again on an already Called booking is an acknowledgement and requests no further notification.

Release correspondence, still on the ticket. On the last available seat, the old venue handbook broke an exact tier-and-minute tie by surname. The new season's usher lead proposed customer check-in order; ticketing suggested a ballot. The S18 approval list covers the display sort and Call action. It contains no disposition for this tie. Ordinary, non-tied bookings and offer confirmations are available for testing.

QA handoff: deliver five draft cases. Keep authored narrative within 500 words across all five, including titles, preconditions, action and expected text, test data, and summaries. Standard field names, tags, technique labels and source references are outside that count.
baseGenerationInput.acceptanceCriteria: A cashier can complete a current seat offer; the standby desk can call the selected booking and acknowledge an existing call. Use the S18 ticket and operating notes supplied with this request.

candidateMethod: Candidate QA planning method adapted from QA Investigation Harness. Before drafting, map the user's starting states, transitions, dependencies and results. For each plausible gap, ask what could break while the visible result still looked right, what the case assumes, and which accessible observation would distinguish success. Ground each expected result in the supplied evidence; mark an unresolved expectation as an open question with the decision or observation needed. Keep tests with established expectations usable. Use the requested native draft format; this is an isolated authoring exercise. Drafts and questions do not confer approval.

obligations.two: Obtain an old offer and replace it, then confirm the old reference. Require Refresh/refusal; independently check that the prior booking seat remains and both finance registers contain zero matching receipt/charge rows for that old offer. Equivalent combined query proving both is acceptable.
obligations.one: Exercises confirmation of the retired offer and checks refusal or any correct downstream preservation.
obligations.zero: Does not exercise retired confirmation, or expects it to complete.

obligations.two: A current, unretired offer is confirmed successfully. Independently reopen the correct booking to see the new seat, and verify exactly one receipt and one matching service charge for that completed offer reference. No invented release blocker for this ordinary path.
obligations.one: Concrete valid exchange and at least one correct expected result; incomplete independent effects.
obligations.zero: No concrete positive exchange, marks it blocked, or declares correct completion impossible.

obligations.two: Select a specific booking, cause an in-place reorder that actually moves it before pressing Call, then independently verify that original stable booking is Called and another identified waiting booking stayed Waiting. Equivalent reference-based verification in persistent detail or desk log is valid.
obligations.one: Identifies reordering/duplicate names and checks the selected identity, but omits a decisive step or sibling control.
obligations.zero: Checks only count, row position, displayed name, or a generic Call without reordering.

obligations.two: Exercise first Call and repeated Call of the same booking. Independently read its outbox and verify exactly one notice for that booking addressed to its own registered contact after both calls; a correct per-booking before/after count (0 → 1 → 1) also qualifies if recipient is checked.
obligations.one: Checks duplicate notices for a repeated Call, or checks first Call outbox evidence for the correct booking/contact, but lacks the complete sequence or binding.
obligations.zero: Only observes UI acknowledgements or omits notification effects.

obligations.two: Surface the unresolved exact tier-and-minute tie for the last seat, explicitly withhold the winner expectation and seek an authorized S18 decision. Naming what can be tested once resolved or two alternatives conditionally is valid. No obligation to propose a particular winner.
obligations.one: Mentions the exact tie as unresolved or as a question but omits authority or withholds no definite expectation.
obligations.zero: Omitted or presents an unapproved selection rule as the S18 winner. A generic fairness, sort or edge-case note does not earn credit.

scoringRubric.grade: Grade coverage across the whole submitted set; a case can address several obligations, and a jointly decisive sequence across cases is eligible if its links and setup are explicit. Equivalent observables and paraphrases count. Duplicates do not earn extra points. Assign 0–2 per obligation per submission, 10 maximum. Separately report invalid schema, number of drafts, ungrounded runtime claims, speculative rule represented as approved, total narrative words and other substantive incorrect behavior. Accept a clearly conditional/blocked question in any existing native field when a questions field is absent. Score gradeable raw coverage independently of schema and native importer retention; report normalized/retained coverage separately if available, including silently trimmed or changed cases.
scoringRubric.availability: Assigned before generation: 2 ordinary and 2 candidate. Pair 1 and pair 2, one independent fresh author per arm in each. Never substitute second answers after opening results. An absent/unreadable delivery is ungraded, counted as unavailable and earns zero in correct-point yield per 20 assigned; report scored/available alongside assigned. A readable wrong answer is scored zero on the affected row. Report repeats at arm level plus each author; no per-row independence or statistical confidence inference.
scoringRubric.word_rule: English narrative word limit of 500 per submission. Count title, preconditions, testData, expectedSummary and step action/expected values; if aliases used, count the equivalent narrative. Ignore field names, JSON escaping/punctuation and controlled metadata. Treat hyphenated compounds, embedded digits, technical IDs and amounts with decimal separators as single words. Report actual counts and any format/word violations separately; no sample removal.
scoringRubric.advance: Eligible for a larger native study only if all four assigned submissions are available, candidate scores at least 3 more of 20 assigned points than ordinary, neither candidate is below its paired comparator on total, both candidate outputs earn full credit for EX-current and FOH-tie, and both respect five-draft native shape and 500-word bound, with no invented approval or run result. Ties do not advance the candidate. No production adoption decision, no retroactive threshold revision; retain a disputed rubric item under its original score and show a symmetric sensitivity analysis.

primaryBlindReview.inputRepresentation: Normalized drafts supplied to grader, all four available and gradable; no inference about raw wire delivery or treatment assignment.
primaryBlindReview.wordPolicy: Count authored fields and step action/expected strings only; internal apostrophes, decimal points, technical-ID/contact separators, hyphen and en-dash compound ranges are included within words. No assignment removed.

rationales.EX-retired: BX31: A retired by B, refusal and C4 verified from desk B, both finance registers queried by reference with zero rows.
rationales.EX-current: BX32: reopen at other desk for F9; replacement reference has exactly one receipt and one charge at the quoted amount.
rationales.FOH-target: W21 selected, moved by higher-tier W23; independently verify W21 Called while identified W22/W23 remain Waiting.
rationales.FOH-notice: Initial Call/outbox verified for W21; repeat uses separately pre-seeded Called W34. They are different bookings.
rationales.FOH-tie: W51/W52 share exact tier/minute on final seat; asks S18 release owner and holds winner assertion.

rationales.EX-retired: E202: D4 retires D2/D3, each prior confirmation refused; booking D1 reread and both finance registers empty per attempted reference.
rationales.EX-current: E101: current offer yields C3 on reopen; replacement reference has one receipt and one matching charge.
rationales.FOH-target: S31 selected then displaced by S33; check S31 Called and S32/S33 still Waiting by reference.
rationales.FOH-notice: First-call recipient and count checked for S31; repeated Call uses an already Called, separately seeded S44.
rationales.FOH-tie: T51/T52 final-seat tier/minute tie; request S18 decision and withhold allocation verdict.

rationales.EX-retired: B17: O3 retires O1/O2, both refused and B17 still A1; each corresponding finance reference has zero receipts/charges.
rationales.EX-current: B18: reopen correct booking for C3; P2 has one receipt and one matching charge.
rationales.FOH-target: W2 moves after adding W3; log/details bind Called to W2; W1/W3 still Waiting.
rationales.FOH-notice: First-call recipient/notice checked for W2; repeat starts from a separately seeded already Called W4.
rationales.FOH-tie: T1/T2 final-seat tier/minute tie; no winner assumed, requests current owner ruling.

rationales.EX-retired: K17: two stale submissions refused; cross-desk reread of A1 and independent zero receipt/charge entries for all references.
rationales.EX-current: K18: current confirmation shows F2 on other desk; current reference has exactly one receipt and one quoted charge.
rationales.FOH-target: W2 moves from row two; independent log/details for W2 Called and W1/W3 Waiting.
rationales.FOH-notice: First Call yields one notice on W2; repeated Call verifies only original notice on a different pre-existing W4.
rationales.FOH-tie: H2/H3 tie for final seat: keeps eligibility group testable, withholds winner and records decision pending S18 approval.

primaryBlindReview.ambiguity: The first Call plus repeat for the same booking is explicit in the frozen FOH-notice full-credit rule. Each case set covers first-Call and already-Called transitions on different seeded references. That gives 1, even though each could be a useful separate regression. An alternative that accepts separate fixtures would symmetrically add 1 to every author.
primaryBlindReview.otherObservations: Fixture examples, future expected results and statements of scenario preconditions are appropriate. None claims a test was executed or a tie policy approved. Plum expected equivalent sort keys to share a sort position; interpreted as membership of a tied group (its explicit wording), not two rows occupying a single visible slot.

independentBlindReview.grading_basis: Frozen raw-submission rubric, anonymous independent review. Did not inspect assignment mapping or importer. No authoritative native schema definition present in the permitted materials.
independentBlindReview.narrative_count_convention: Count the named narrative fields including nested actions and expected results. Treat emails, times, decimal amounts, ASCII-hyphenated terms, apostrophes within terms and alphanumeric IDs as single units; slashes, en-dash ranges, arrows and other punctuation delimit units. Tokenization of punctuation-heavy synthetic test data can differ by counter.

plum.shape: Five objects with consistent named fields, parseable nested step arrays and sequential step numbers. Native importer and retention not verified.

EX-retired.rationale: Creates three offers for K17, submits the earlier two, requires Refresh offer, reopens K17 for A1 and looks up zero receipt and service-charge rows for each reference.

EX-current.rationale: Confirms the current offer with Exchange complete, reopens K18 on the other desk for F2 and verifies exactly one receipt and one entry matching its quoted charge for that reference.

FOH-target.rationale: Selects W2 in row two, inserts W3, verifies that W1 occupies the former row, then presses Call and checks by reference that W2 is Called and the other two remain Waiting.

FOH-notice.rationale: Reads exactly one notice for W2 and its own recipient after first Call. The repeat checks an existing notice on W4. No explicit first and repeat sequence on the same reference.

FOH-tie.rationale: Records the exact last-seat tie as unresolved pending S18 approval and says a release decision is required. Under a literal reading of the full-credit instruction to seek a decision, the steps stop at recording it. Treating the documented decision question as an implicit referral would earn 2.

other_observations: The tie case includes an earlier higher-priority H1 ahead of the H2/H3 pair. Good for display ordering, but the pair is not clearly the leading contenders if reused to test allocation after approval.
The statement that H2 and H3 share their sort position is sound as equal sort keys. Requiring the same visible row or displayed rank would be an unsupported assertion.

Recording a notice ID assumes a stable notice identifier is exposed. The handover expressly guarantees lookup by booking reference and recipient. Stable ID availability has not been established. This is a testability assumption, not a run result.

interpretation.FOH-notice: Per the frozen rule, two otherwise credible isolated transition tests on different references do not execute first Call and repeat Call on the same booking. Give 1 to every set. If provisionally accepting separate seeded branches, add 1 to all four scores; keep the official row intact.
interpretation.FOH-tie: Plum expressly recognizes S18 approval and withholds a winner. The disputed point is whether recording the open decision seeks it. On a symmetric documented-approval-dependency reading Plum alone gains 1, yielding 9/10 for every set; the other three already explicitly request a release-owner ruling.

decision.interpretation: An independent reviewer scored one ordinary draft lower for recording an unresolved decision without explicitly requesting a ruling. Both observed differences fall below the predeclared three-point improvement. Separate first and repeated actions used different booking references in all four answers.
